UPPER-DIVISION UNDERGRADUATE PHYSICS / E&M II

Can energy cross an empty gap?

Follow the fields from a charging capacitor to a transparent coating. Use Maxwell’s equations to predict what changes, what is conserved, and what an experiment would need to measure.

01 / EXPLORE A MODEL

When does a film
stop reflecting?

An ideal film between air and glass cancels reflection near its design wavelength. Keep the film fixed and move the wavelength. Then vary its thickness and predict where the minimum shifts.

Film controls

Fixed indices 1.00 → √1.5 → 1.50. Normal incidence. Lossless and nondispersive. The bare interface reflects 4%.

REFLECTANCE—
TRANSMITTANCE—
FIRST MINIMUM—

The solid line shows the coated interface. The dashed line shows bare glass.

Model equation and assumptions

Reflectance is |r|². The lab independently solves the four tangential-field boundary equations and checks the power balance.

03 / COMPUTE & CHECK

Run your own
field calculations.

Use vector calculus and complex amplitudes to make quantitative predictions. Four worked investigations connect the video questions to model checks.

Electrodynamics Python lab

Compare the capacitor energy budget, integrate solenoid fields, check continuity in a taper, and vary the thickness of a coating.

Launch JupyterLite ↗

First launch needs network access. If asked, choose Python (Pyodide). Use Run → Run All Cells, then download your notebook to keep your changes.

Download notebook ↓

How to investigate

  1. Predict a direction, sign or limiting value.
  2. Compute it independently in two ways.
  3. Change one parameter and explain the result.
  4. Use a convergence or sensitivity check.
  5. State what a real measurement could test.

04 / CHECK YOUR REASONING

Practice without
the video.

Each standalone H5P question gives feedback and a retry. Explain why the distractors fail, then revisit the matching notebook investigation.

These original formative activities draw on learning goals in the CURrENT study. Their scores serve as practice feedback. The site does not store individual grades.

05 / INDEPENDENT TRANSFER

Design a coating
for an unfamiliar substrate.

A sensor window has index 2.25. Your available film has index 1.40. Choose a thickness that controls reflection over 450–650 nm with a manufacturing tolerance of ±8 nm.

Derive the ideal match.

Use both boundary conditions. Compare the ideal film with the available material.

Optimize a real constraint.

Minimize the worst reflectance over the wavelength band and thickness uncertainty.

Defend the model.

Check numerical convergence, compare against bare glass, and propose a measurement.

SOURCES & SCOPE

Research and assumptions

Conceptual learning goals draw on C. Baily, Q. X. Ryan, C. Astolfi, and S. J. Pollock, “Conceptual assessment tool for advanced undergraduate electrodynamics,” Phys. Rev. Phys. Educ. Res. 13, 020113 (2017). This module uses original formative questions.

Scientific background: MIT 8.02T notes. Prerequisites are introductory E&M, vector calculus, complex numbers and basic Python. The module treats selected E&M II ideas in SI, with explicit idealizations in the lecture and lab.
